The nearest candidate, "Microscopic black holes evaporate essentially instantly through Hawking radiation," restricts to a mass regime and asserts a timescale predicate. Whether micro-black-hole evaporation is essentially instant depends on the mass-scaling of the evaporation time, a consideration with no bearing on whether stellar-mass black holes emit Hawking radiation at all; conversely, evidence about the general effect would bear on that claim only through an additional premise. Different implicit parameter, different decomposition: a specification, not a match. And the existence debate the source participates in is hosted on no node at all. Minting the general claim and recording the relationship is the recoverable choice.

On stance: the source asserts the proposition's reality by way of reporting consensus ("broad consensus among physicists on the reality of Hawking radiation"), while flagging the absence of direct experimental evidence. Judged against the canonical direction, that is an assertion of the claim, recorded as "affirms" with the reduced-confidence caveat noted, not "poses," since the sentence takes the reality of the effect as given and reports where the evidence gap lies.

The nearest candidate turns on an additional consideration, the mass-dependent timescale of evaporation, so its decomposition differs from the proposed claim's: the evaporation-timescale proposition is a specification of the existence claim, not the same claim under different wording. A source denying the general proposition would not thereby deny the timescale claim, and the two would unfold differently in argument. No node hosts the general existence proposition or its negation, and the negation search confirms no mirror-page exists. Per the preference for the recoverable error, this is a new claim.
